chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Abdul-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Jaloudi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Mu'ammar told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Dahir al-Ahmari told us, saying: My father told me, saying: Al-A'mash told us, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that Umar ibn al-Khattab used to recite: 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.'
Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said: The Family of Yasin is the Family of Muhammad, peace be upon them.
ai.seo_question: Who is the Family of Yasin mentioned in the Quran?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* establishes the identity of 'Al Yasin' as the Prophet's Household (Ahl al-Bayt) through the practice of Umar ibn al-Khattab, who recited 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin' during prayers. This interpretation is significant in Shia scholarship as it links the Quranic phrase directly to the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing their spiritual status and the continuity of prophetic tradition. The hadith highlights the early recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt's unique position within the Islamic community.
